body:
Six defects in the React operator HMI (`src/p1am_control_system/frontend`), all of which could mislead a human standing next to live hardware — a P1AM PLC, a DC power supply and heaters driven from a Raspberry Pi touchscreen.

Every fix was written test-first: the test was added, watched fail against the current code, and only then fixed.

Closes #3996
Closes #4010
Closes #4011
Closes #4013
Closes #4020
Closes #4042

---

### #4010 (P0) — HMI reported CONNECTED on a dead backend

**Defect.** Every field of `telemetryFrameSchema` is `.optional()`, so `safeParse({})` succeeds. `useTelemetryStream.applyFrame` treated any successful parse as a live frame: it stamped `lastFrameAt` and set `isConnected(true)` even for an empty payload. On the backend, `latest_frame` starts as `{}` and is only reassigned on a _successful_ poll — never cleared, never aged, always HTTP 200.

**Operator-visible consequence.** The poll loop dies, the header stays green CONNECTED, and the trend appends the same frozen value forever — which renders as a beautifully stable process. The operator reads a rock-steady value that stopped updating twenty minutes ago and acts on it.

**Fix.** Liveness now requires content, and is expressed as an age rather than a boolean:

- `hasTelemetryContent()` requires at least one _recognised_ field (`tags`, `power_supply`, `temperature`, …). An empty object is not a frame, and neither is a payload of unknown keys.
- The hook exposes `dataAgeMs` and `freshness` (`live` / `stale` / `offline`), driven by a clock that keeps ticking when nothing arrives — an age advanced only by incoming frames would freeze exactly when it matters. `isConnected` is now derived (`freshness === "live"`), so an open socket with no data no longer claims the process is live.
- The header renders `DataAgeIndicator` — "STALE DATA · 20 m 4 s ago" cannot be misread as healthy.
- `data-freshness` on the dashboard root greys and cross-hatches every live process readout past the threshold, so a **frozen** value is visually distinct from a **steady** one. This is the property the old boolean design could not express.

**Tests.** `lib/dataAge.test.ts` (age-to-band mapping, incl. DbC on negative/non-finite ages); `hooks/useTelemetryStream.test.ts` — empty payload is not live, unrecognised-fields payload is not live, a frozen stream ages out of CONNECTED under fake timers, an open socket alone is not data; `api/schemas.test.ts::hasTelemetryContent`; `components/DataAgeIndicator.test.tsx`.

**Backend follow-up (not this PR).** The backend should also stamp `frame_ts` on each frame and serve **503** from `/api/snapshot` when the cached frame is stale, rather than always returning 200 with a never-cleared payload. This PR implements the client side defensively only; no Python was touched.

### #4011 (P0) — one malformed alarm suppressed the ENTIRE alarm list

**Defect.** `.catch(undefined)` sat on the whole `active_alarms` record, not on each entry. One bad alarm object turned the entire map into `undefined`, `if (frame.active_alarms)` went false, and `setActiveAlarms` was never called again.

**Operator-visible consequence.** The UI keeps rendering its last list — including "All normal — no active alarms" — while alarms fire on the PLC. Silent and permanent for the session, because nothing else polled `/api/alarms/active`.

> **Note:** a **passing test previously asserted this defect as correct behaviour.** `schemas.test.ts` contained "does NOT reject the whole frame when one field is malformed", which explicitly expected `parsed.data.active_alarms` to be `undefined` when one entry was garbage. That test has been rewritten: the frame-level resilience assertion is kept, and the alarm-map assertion now demands the good entries survive.

**Fix.**

- `.catch` moved to the element level (`activeAlarmEntrySchema`), so one bad alarm costs you that alarm. `partitionAlarmMap()` splits survivors from dropped ids.
- `droppedAlarmCount` is surfaced and `AlarmsHeader` raises a visible degraded-data banner ("Alarm data incomplete — N alarms could not be read … Check the PLC alarm summary directly"). The reassuring "All normal" summary is suppressed while data is known-missing.
- A periodic `/api/alarms/active` + `/api/events` reconciliation poll gives the list a recovery path independent of the stream, and clears the degraded flag when it returns a complete list.

**Tests.** `api/schemas.test.ts` — drops only the malformed alarm, `partitionAlarmMap` cases; `useTelemetryStream.test.ts` — good alarms survive a bad entry, drop count clears on a clean frame, an empty map means "cleared" not "no update"; `components/AlarmsHeader.test.tsx`.

### #4013 (P0) — Alicat setpoint entry overwritten while the operator types

**Defect.** An effect keyed on `[inspectorView, alicats]` reset the controlled setpoint input to the device value. `alicats` gets a new reference on essentially every frame because `shallowListEqual` compares live analog fields (`mass_flow`, `pressure`, `temperature`) that change every scan on real hardware.

**Operator-visible consequence.** The field fights every keystroke. Pressing Set can commit a partially-reverted value — 2 instead of 25 — which `AlicatInspector` accepts because it is in range. A tenfold gas-flow error with no indication.

**Fix.** New `useSetpointDraft` hook: seed from the device while untouched, hand ownership to the operator on the first keystroke, re-seed only when the entry is scoped to a **different device id** (a scalar — keying on an object that changes reference every frame is the original defect). This is the `operatorTouchedRef` pattern already used by `TemperatureControl`, shared via the pure `seedDraftText` helper. The live device setpoint is now a separate read-only readout with a "Pending — entry differs from the device setpoint" cue, so both values are visible instead of fighting over one widget.

**Tests.** `hooks/useSetpointDraft.test.ts` — five frames with drifting live values land mid-entry and the draft does not budge; scope change re-seeds; `components/AlicatInspector.test.tsx`; `lib/operatorDraft.test.ts`.

### #4020 (P1) — power supply +/- commanded from a stale staged value

**Defect.** `stagedSetpointText` was initialised to `"0"` and never seeded from `liveStatus.setpoint_a`, while `nudgeSetpoint` computed `staged + delta` and called `applySetpoint` **immediately** — contradicting the file's own documented contract at line 31: _"Apply commits the staged value — typing alone commands nothing."_

**Operator-visible consequence.** Supply running at 30 A, operator reloads the HMI (kiosk refresh): the box reads 0 while telemetry correctly shows 30.00 A. One tap of `+` commands 1 A, collapsing the output by 29 A with no confirmation.

**Fix.** The staged entry uses `useSetpointDraft` seeded from `liveStatus.setpoint_a` and re-seeds while untouched. The `+` and `−` buttons adjust the **staged** value only; Apply is restored as the sole write path.

**Tests.** `components/PowerSupplyControl.test.tsx` — seeds to `30.00` rather than `0`; `+` stages `31.00` and issues **zero** POSTs to `/api/power_supply/setpoint`; a later frame does not yank a staged value; staging clamps at zero; Apply is what writes.

### #4042 (P2) — two smaller correctness defects

**(a) Event log never fetched on mount or polled.** `fetchAlarmsAndEvents` was the only writer of `eventsHistory` and its only call site was inside `handleAcknowledgeAlarm`; the mount effect omitted it and there was no interval. The Events tab was blank until an unrelated acknowledgement happened, then frozen. Fixed with a new `usePollingRefresh` hook (mount + 15 s interval), which doubles as #4011's recovery path. Tested in `hooks/usePollingRefresh.test.ts`, including that a callback recreated on every render does not reset the timer — a naive dependency there would mean the poll never fires.

**(b) Approaching-alarm cue computed from the uncommitted draft.** The highlights came from `configDraft`, the local half-typed draft, and `ConfigField` wrote `Number.parseFloat(e.target.value)` straight into it — so clearing the field stored `NaN`, and `x >= 0.9 * NaN` is **false**, switching the pre-alarm cue **off** while the supply was still climbing. Warnings now come from the server-enforced `config`, via `approachingLimit()` which deliberately fails **loud** (an unusable limit warns rather than reassures), and `parseConfigNumber()` rejects non-finite input. Tested in `PowerSupplyControl.test.tsx`.

### #3996 (P1) — none of this was gated

`package.json` defines `build` (`tsc && vite build`), `lint` and `test` (`vitest run`), and **no workflow ran any of them** — `grep -rn "p1am_control_system/frontend" .github/workflows/` returned nothing. The vitest suite covers the API client, the payload schemas, explorer state and the plot components — exactly the parts that would mislead an operator — and never executed.

Adds `.github/workflows/p1am-frontend.yml`: path-filtered to `src/p1am_control_system/frontend/**` and the workflow itself, pinned to `runs-on: [d-sorg-fleet, Linux]`, running `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run test`.

**Making the gate useful required repairing the existing suite first.** 15 tests across `panelLayout`, `usePanelLayout` and `PanelStack` were already failing with `localStorage.clear is not a function`: Node >= 22 exposes its own experimental `localStorage` global, so vitest's jsdom environment does not install jsdom's `Storage` over it, and the object Node returns implements no Storage methods. `src/test/setup.ts` now installs a spec-shaped in-memory Storage when the host's is unusable — the HMI genuinely persists operator layout and theme in Web Storage, so these tests must run regardless of the runner's Node version.

---

### Verification

```
npm run lint   -> 0 errors (2 pre-existing exhaustive-deps warnings, unchanged)
npm run build  -> tsc clean, vite build OK
npm run test   -> 52 files, 444 tests, all passing  (was 44 files / 381 tests with 15 failing)
```

### Notes and things left undone

- **No Python was touched.** The `frame_ts` / 503-when-stale change described under #4010 is a backend concern and belongs to another PR; the client side here degrades safely without it.
- `App.tsx` was 1690 lines, 190 over the repo's 1500-line source budget, and the pre-commit guardrail blocks any edit to an over-budget file. The self-contained PID-tuning/MPC tab is extracted verbatim to `components/TuningPanel.tsx`, bringing `App.tsx` to 1421. No behaviour change.
- **DRY gap left open:** `TemperatureControl.recallSetpointText` still carries its own copy of the seeding logic that `lib/operatorDraft.ts` now owns. Folding it over is a one-line change, but that file is 1975 lines — 475 over budget — so any edit to it fails the same guardrail until it is split. Noted in the helper's docstring.

## Summary

Three defects in the safety-critical control math behind `/api/pid/{i}/tuning/stop` and `/api/mpc/simulate`. Each was reproduced with a failing test before any production code was touched.

Closes #4018
Closes #4039
Refs #4033

**The Cohen-Coon coefficient formulas were checked against Cohen & Coon (1953) and deliberately left alone.** `Kc = (1/Kp)(tau/theta)(4/3 + theta/4tau)`, `Ti = theta(32+6r)/(13+8r)`, `Td = 4theta/(11+2r)` at `pid_tuning.py:47-55` and `:122-129` are correct as written. `test_cohen_coon_matches_reference` and `test_cohen_coon_pinned_values` still pass unchanged, pinning them.

---

## #4018(a) — negative gains clamped to zero, reported as success

`as_response()` clamped every recommended gain with `max(0.0, ...)`. `cohen_coon_pid` correctly returns **negative** gains for a reverse-acting process (identified `Kp < 0`); the clamp turned them into `kp=0, ki=0, kd=0` and still reported `"Tuning parameters identified successfully"` — an open-loop controller presented as a tuned one.

Failing test first (`test_response_preserves_negative_gains`, building a `TuningResult` with genuinely negative gains):

```
E   assert 0.0 == -2.125 ± 2.1e-06
      Obtained: 0.0
      Expected: -2.125 ± 2.1e-06
```

Fixed by dropping the clamp. An identified `Kp < 0` now yields `status="warning"` with a message naming the reverse-acting process and instructing that the loop be configured reverse-acting before the gains are applied.

## #4018(b) — under-resolved dead time inflated the recommendation

`theta_ident = max(MIN_TIME_PARAM, t_10 - step_time)` had no noise rejection and no minimum-sample check. A noisy PV sample lands the first crossing on the step sample itself, `theta` hits the `0.1` floor, and since `Kc` scales with `tau/theta` the recommendation explodes — and was returned as `"success"`.

Reproduced with a single-sample noise spike at the instant of the step (`test_noise_spike_at_step_sample_is_rejected`): the plant needs `Kc ~ 2.1`, the floored theta produced `Kc ~ 87`, status `"success"`.

Now:

- **Rejected** (zero gains, `status="warning"`) when the first crossing falls within 2 sample intervals of the step, when both thresholds are crossed on the same sample, when the PV never responds or never crosses the thresholds, or when `|Kp|` is too small to invert. The sample interval is taken as the median of the recorded timestamp deltas rather than assumed.
- **Downgraded** to `status="warning"` while still reporting gains when theta lands on the `MIN_TIME_PARAM` floor, when the step was below the measurable minimum, when the dead-time ratio falls outside the published Cohen-Coon validity band `0.1 <= theta/tau <= 1.0`, or when a gain exceeds a `MAX_REC_GAIN` sanity bound.

## #4018(c) — 10%/63.2% pair biased the identification

Switched to the published two-point method: the 28.3% and 63.2% crossings sit at `theta + tau/3` and `theta + tau`, giving `tau = 1.5*(t63 - t28)` and `theta = t63 - tau`. The old 10% crossing sits at `theta + 0.105*tau`, biasing theta high and tau low by ~`0.105*tau` each.

Failing test first (`test_two_point_identification_uses_28_percent_pair`, plant `Kp=2, tau=10, theta=3`):

```
E   assert 8.5 == 10.0 ± 0.5      # tau, old 10% pair
```

After: `tau=9.75` (was 8.5, -15%), `theta=3.25` (was 4.5, +50%).

## #4039 — MPC mixed absolute and incremental moves

`free_response` already contains the full predicted effect of holding `last_u`, but the decision variable was initialised to the absolute CV (`u_opt = [last_u] * control_horizon`), multiplied by the step-response dynamic matrix as if it were a move vector, then clamped and applied as an absolute CV. The current input was counted twice.

The optimizer is extracted into `solve_dmc_move()` first as a **pure refactor** — verified byte-identical output across 6 parameter combinations before any behaviour change — so the defect could be tested directly. Failing test first (`test_steady_state_move_is_zero`): with `pv == setpoint` and `last_cv` already holding the process there, the optimal move must be zero.

```
E   assert -12.904843309648992 == 0.0 ± 1.0e-09   # setpoint 50
E   assert  -5.161937323859604 == 0.0 ± 1.0e-09   # setpoint 20
E   assert -20.647749295775186 == 0.0 ± 1.0e-09   # setpoint 80
```

The demanded move scaled with the operating point — the signature of a double-counted input. Now solves for delta-u from a zero origin, bounds the **moves**, and the caller applies `mpc_cv[k] = clamp(last_u + delta_u[0], 0, 100)`.

Effect on the comparison chart (`Kp=1.2`, final CV/PV of the MPC trace):

| setpoint | correct CV | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 16.67 | 8.11 (PV 9.73) | 16.81 (PV 19.73) |
| 50 | 41.67 | 20.26 (PV 24.31) | 42.02 (PV 49.34) |
| 80 | 66.67 | 32.42 (PV 38.90) | 67.20 (PV 78.96) |

MPC settled at roughly half the required CV at every operating point; it now lands within ~1%.

## #4033 — the clamp test was vacuous

`test_response_shape_clamps_negative_gains` called `identify_fopdt_and_tune` with `step_triggered=False`, which takes the warning branch and makes `rec_*` zero by construction — the assertion held with the clamp removed, so it never guarded anything. Replaced by `test_response_preserves_negative_gains` (constructs a `TuningResult` with negative gains directly, asserts gains preserved, status warning, message names reverse-acting) plus `test_reverse_acting_process_is_flagged_not_zeroed` covering the same contract end-to-end from a synthetic reverse-acting step. The remaining shape assertions were kept as `test_response_shape_is_stable`.

## Verification

- 52 tests in `test_pid_tuning_math.py` + new `test_mpc_dmc.py`, all passing. Every new behavioural test was written and observed failing against the old code first.
- Full backend suite: **914 passed**, 1 pre-existing-expectation failure (see below).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` clean on all four touched files.
- DbC applied throughout: `identify_fopdt_and_tune`, `solve_dmc_move`, and `TuningResult.__post_init__` validate types (`TypeError`) and ranges (`ValueError`), with preconditions documented in docstrings. The numeric guards live once in `pid_tuning` and are imported by `mpc` (which already depended on it) rather than duplicated.

## Known follow-up outside this PR's file scope

`src/p1am_control_system/backend/tests/test_backend_p1am_safety.py::test_pid_tuning_stop_recommends_expected_pid_for_fixed_history` now fails. Its 12-sample fixture has PV values `11.0` and `16.32` that are *exactly* the old 10% and 63.2% thresholds, and it is sampled at 1 s with only two transient points. The new guard correctly rejects it:

> Tuning rejected: the process crossed the 28.3% threshold 1.50 s after the step, less than 2 sample interval (1.00 s) spans.

This is the "affected test expectation" #4018 anticipated, but that file is owned by another agent in this drive so I did not touch it. It needs either the expectation changed to `status == "warning"`, or the fixture replaced with a properly sampled response. A verified replacement for the same plant (`Kp=1, tau=1, theta=0.5`, dt=0.1) yields `status="success"`, `parameters={"kp": 1.0, "tau": 0.9, "theta": 0.6}`, `recommended_pid={"kp": 2.249, "ki": 1.909, "kd": 0.438}`.

Also noted: `.gitignore` covers `src/p1am_control_system/backend/dcs_scada.db` but not a root-level `dcs_scada.db`, which the backend tests create when pytest runs from the repo root.

body:
Closes #3995.

The P1AM firmware owns the safety interlock, the four PID loops, and the analog/relay outputs — it is what keeps the plant safe when the Raspberry Pi host is gone. Nothing in CI compiled it and nothing ran its tests.

## What was already there, and why it stopped working

A host-side harness existed at `tests/p1am_control_system/firmware/`: a Makefile that builds the **real** firmware sources against a fake `HardwareInterface`, with assertions covering scaling, anti-windup, trip latching and NaN soft-fail. It sits inside a directory CI does collect (`ci-standard.yml:701` adds `tests/p1am_control_system/`) but holds no `.py` files, so pytest walked straight past it.

Never being run, it rotted until it no longer compiled:

- `MockHardware` did not implement `WriteHeaterRelay`, so the class was abstract and every `MockHardware hw;` was a hard error.
- The `StorageManager` round-trip still used the pre-lolo/hihi **4-argument** `Save`/`Load`; the real signature took 6 once `InterlockConfigData` grew to four limits (`kMagic` bumped 0xDC51 → 0xDC52).
- `TestSignalBroker` asserted 350 °C → 35.0 %, an expectation left over from a 1000 °C full scale. The firmware moved to 1400 °C, making the correct answer 25.0 %.

That last one is the interesting failure: the suite was not merely unbuilt, it encoded a **stale physical constant**. This is the class of drift the harness exists to catch.

## Changes

**Harness repair**
- `MockHardware` implements the full interface. It additionally records the highest value each analog output was ever commanded to, so a safety test can assert an output was *never energized* rather than merely reading zero at the end — the distinction that matters for the watchdog and E-stop work in #3999/#4002.
- The `StorageManager` test round-trips all four interlock tiers and asserts an untouched tag keeps its saved value, so a future struct change cannot silently drop lolo/hihi the way the last one did.
- `test_dcs.cpp` now `#error`s under `NDEBUG`. Every check in the suite is an `assert()`; a build that compiled them away would exit 0 having tested nothing.

**DRY fix that makes the stale assertion impossible to repeat**
- `kThermocoupleFullScaleC` moves from a function-local literal in `SignalBroker.cpp` to a public `static constexpr` in `SignalBroker.h`. The test derives its expected percentage from that constant instead of hardcoding one — hardcoding is exactly what let the assertion go stale. This also gives the backend cross-check in #3998 a single named definition to read against.

**CI**
- New `.github/workflows/p1am-firmware.yml`, path-filtered to the firmware and its tests, pinned to `[d-sorg-fleet, Linux]` (the pool is heterogeneous and the Makefile needs a POSIX toolchain):
  - `firmware-unit-tests` — plain `g++`, no board toolchain, runs in seconds. This is the TDD vehicle for the rest of the firmware cluster.
  - `firmware-compile` — `arduino-cli` against the real `P1AM-100:samd` package, catching library and signature breakage the host harness cannot see (it never includes `P1AM.h` or `Ethernet.h`).
- The unit-test job greps the binary's own success line rather than trusting the exit code, so a build that silently tested nothing still fails.
- Toolchain versions are written to the job summary each run, so a firmware binary can be traced to the toolchain that produced it.

**Housekeeping**
- `.gitignore` for `*.o`, `test_dcs`, and `config.bin` (StorageManager persists to it when exercised on the host), so a local `make test` cannot dirty the tree.

## Verification

Built and run under WSL Ubuntu-22.04, g++ 11.4:

```
=== DCS CORE FIRMWARE TDD TEST RUNNER ===
TestSignalBroker PASSED!
TestPIDController PASSED!
TestSafetyInterlock PASSED!
TestStorageManager PASSED!
TestSoftFailRuntimeContracts PASSED!
All C++ Core Firmware Tests Passed Successfully!
```

No Python or frontend code is touched.

## Follow-on

This PR deliberately does **not** fix any firmware behaviour — it only makes the firmware testable and gated. The defects the harness now protects against are next, each with a failing test written first:

- #3999 comms watchdog
- #4001 trip tier, unrouted tags, `ClearTrip` reachability
- #4002 PID integral reset on setpoint change
- #4032 tag clamp versus interlock limit domain

One gap this PR exposes and does not close: `SafetyInterlock::Evaluate` reads only `high_limits_`/`low_limits_`, and the harness only ever exercised those — nothing tests the HIHI/LOLO tier because nothing evaluates it. That is #4001's job.
